statement: Spot HBM3E modules are reported to sell at roughly four to five times the long-term-agreement price, indicating an extremely thin uncontracted memory channel.
why: A spot price several times the contract price is the classic signature of near-zero available channel inventory; buyers without a long-term agreement are paying scarcity rents.

impact.mechanism: Depleted uncontracted memory inventory raises the bill-of-materials cost and lengthens practical availability for accelerator builders who are not party to a long-term agreement.

evidence.excerpt: A 36GB HBM3E module reportedly sells for about 2.87 million won (around $2,100) on the spot market, compared with just 500,000 to 700,000 won ($300 to $400) under long-term agreements

confidence.basis: Secondary trade-press reporting of spot pricing, hedged with 'reportedly' in the source; no primary price index fetched.

dispersion: Spot roughly $2,100 per 36GB module versus $300-$400 under long-term agreement, a four-to-five times gap.
